COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Jane Luu is an astronomer. Luu (Vietnamese: Lưu Lệ Hằng; born July 1963) is a Vietnamese-American astronomer and defense systems engineer.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Ted Kaczynski is a mathematician. The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing) before his identity was known, resulting in the media naming him the "Unabomber".
What is the atomic number of Indium?
Indium: It is a silvery-white post-transition metal and one of the softest elements.
What is the atomic number of Scandium?
Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
In what year was Aristotle born?
Aristotle (Ancient Greek: Ἀριστοτέλης, romanized: Aristotélēs; 384–322 BC) was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath.
In what year was Polyester discovered?
Polyester is a category of polymers that contain one or two ester linkages in every repeat unit of their main chain.
Information theory: Claude Shannon. Information theory is the mathematical study of the quantification, storage, and communication of a particular type of mathematically defined information.
Midazolam: Pfizer. It induces sleepiness, decreases anxiety, and causes anterograde amnesia.
In which country did the CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder take place?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: People's Republic of China. The JF-17 can be used for multiple roles, including interception, ground attack, anti-ship, and aerial reconnaissance.
Who is credited with discovering Darmstadtium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Darmstadtium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
Who is credited with discovering 2 Pallas?
2 Pallas: Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers. Pallas (minor-planet designation: 2 Pallas) is the third-largest asteroid in the Solar System by volume and mass.
Who is credited with discovering Multiple sclerosis?
Multiple sclerosis: Jean-Martin Charcot. It is a type of demyelinating disease, where the nervous system's ability to transmit signals is damaged.
Which European four-engine turboprop military transport plane, sized between the Lockheed C-130 and Boeing C-17, can land on rough airstrips and double as an aerial refueling tanker?
Airbus A400M Atlas is a European four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft. It can carry heavier loads than the C-130 and can use rough landing strips.
Before sharing the 2010 Nobel for graphene, this Manchester physicist won an Ig Nobel for levitating a frog using its own magnetism — who is he?
Andre Geim (born 21 October 1958) is a Russian-born British physicist working in England in the School of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Manchester.
Which noble gas, symbol Ar and atomic number 18, is the third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere — more plentiful there than carbon dioxide or neon?
Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
This facial hair grows on the jaw, chin, and cheeks, most commonly in adult men, though some women develop it too in a condition called hirsutism — name it?
Beard is the hair that grows on the jaw, chin, upper lip, lower lip, cheeks, and neck of humans and some non-human animals.
Dermatologists call the small version of this fluid-filled skin pocket a vesicle and the larger version a bulla; its English name traces back to an Old French word for a leprous nodule. What is it?

Blister is a small pocket of body fluid (lymph, serum, plasma, blood, or pus) within the upper layers of the skin, usually caused by forceful rubbing (friction), burning, freezing, chemical exposure or infection.
This English guard-dog breed combines the size of the Mastiff with genes from the extinct Old English Bulldog, and gained Kennel Club recognition in 1924 — which breed?
Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
Which Mediterranean evergreen tree, grown mainly in Spain, produces edible seed pods often ground into a chocolate substitute, with seeds that yield a gum used as a food thickener?
Carob (Ceratonia siliqua) is a flowering evergreen tree or shrub in the Caesalpinioideae subfamily of the legume family, Fabaceae.
This class of jawed fish — including sharks and rays — has a skeleton made almost entirely of cartilage, setting it apart from its bony-skeletoned relatives. What class is this?

Chondrichthyes (from Ancient Greek (khndros) 'cartilage' and (ikhths) 'fish') is a class of jawed fish that contains the cartilaginous fish or chondrichthyans, which all have skeletons primarily composed of cartilage.
This towering annual in the daisy family yields seeds in two flavors — oilseed (the world's fourth most-used vegetable oil) and the confectionary kind you crack as a snack — which plant?
Common sunflower (Helianthus annuus) is a large annual forb in the daisy family Asteraceae.
This term describes all the material inside a cell's outer membrane, excluding the nucleus (in cells that have one) — its main components include a gel-like fluid called the cytosol. What is it?
Cytoplasm is all the material within a eukaryotic or prokaryotic cell, enclosed by the cell membrane, including the organelles and excluding the nucleus in eukaryotic cells.
Tamed in Africa millennia ago and still hauling loads across the developing world, which equine traces its lineage to Equus africanus?
Donkey is a domesticated equine. It was domesticated in Africa some 5000–7000 years ago, and has been used mainly as a working animal since that time.
The tallest native bird in Australia and the third-tallest living bird overall, this flightless ratite can grow up to 1.9 metres tall. What bird is it?
Emu (Dromaius novaehollandiae) is a species of flightless bird endemic to Australia, where it is the tallest native bird.

Mostly caused by a mutation in the PRNP gene, this neurodegenerative prion disease begins with gradually worsening sleep trouble and progresses to total sleeplessness, speech and coordination problems, and death within months — which disease?
Fatal insomnia is a neurodegenerative prion disease that results in trouble sleeping as its hallmark symptom.
Named after a German militant group in a reader's 1994 letter and formalized by a Stanford linguist in 2005, this cognitive bias makes newly learned facts seem suddenly everywhere — what is it?

Frequency illusion (also known as the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon or Red Car Theory) is a cognitive bias in which a person notices a specific concept, word, or product more frequently after recently becoming aware of it.
Caused in over 90% of cases by iodine deficiency, this visible swelling in the neck comes from an enlarged thyroid gland — name the condition?
Goitre (British English, spelled goiter in American English) is a swelling in the neck resulting from an enlarged thyroid gland.
A Hollywood star of Algiers and Boom Town, this Austrian-American actress also co-invented a wartime radio guidance system — who was she?
Hedy Lamarr (born Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler; November 9, 1914 - January 19, 2000) was an Austrian and American actress and inventor.

This condition occurs when cerebrospinal fluid builds up in and around the brain, in babies causing a rapid increase in head size and in the elderly causing poor balance and mental decline — what condition is it?
Hydrocephalus is a condition in which cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) builds up within and/or around the brain, which can cause pressure to increase in the skull.

This sudden bleeding into brain tissue or its ventricles is one of two major stroke categories, alongside the blockage-caused kind, and can trigger headache, one-sided weakness, or sudden speech and vision problems — what's the condition?
Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), also known as hemorrhagic stroke, is a sudden bleeding into the tissues of the brain (i.e., the parenchyma), into its ventricles, or both.
England's very first Astronomer Royal, he compiled a 3,000-star catalogue and even spotted Uranus — though he mistakenly logged it as a star. Who was he?
John Flamsteed (19 August 1646 - 31 December 1719) was an English astronomer and the first Astronomer Royal.
Native to southern China but long cultivated in Japan and Southeast Asia, this small fruit closely resembles an orange in color and texture but is only about the size of a large olive — what is it?
Kumquat are a group of small, angiosperm, fruit-bearing trees in the family Rutaceae.
Sociable for a big cat and more active by day than its relatives, this savannah hunter is so sexually dimorphic that only the males grow a sweeping mane. Which animal?
Lion (Panthera leo) is a large cat of the genus Panthera, currently ranging only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India.

This German sexologist founded the Scientific-Humanitarian Committee, which carried out what's been called the first advocacy for homosexual and transgender rights — before the Nazis stripped his citizenship in 1933. Who was he?
Magnus Hirschfeld (14 May 1868 - 14 May 1935) was a German physician, sexologist, and LGBTQ advocate whose German citizenship was revoked in 1933 by the Nazi government.
This natural biological transition marks the permanent end of menstrual periods, typically occurring between ages 45 and 55 as estrogen levels decline — what is it?
Menopause is the time when menstrual periods permanently stop, marking the end of the reproductive stage for the female human.
This Nissin Food Products founder invented instant chicken ramen and went on to create the Top Ramen and Cup Noodles brands — who is he?

Momofuku Ando (March 5, 1910 - January 5, 2007), born Go Pek-Hok (Peh-e-j: G Pek-hok; Ti-l: Go Pik-hok), was a Taiwanese-born, ethnic Chinese, Japanese inventor and businessman who founded Nissin Food Products Co., Ltd.

Distinguished from flatworms by having a digestive tract with openings at both ends, these free-living or parasitic roundworms make up their own entire phylum found in nearly every environment on Earth — what are they?
Nematode (or NEEM-; Ancient), roundworms or eelworms constitute the phylum Nematoda.
Founder of the charity Volnoe Delo and the industrial group Basic Element, which Russian oligarch led both En+ Group and Rusal until stepping down in 2018?
Oleg Deripaska (born 2 January 1968) is a Russian oligarch and billionaire.

Closely related to carrot and parsley, this pale, long-tapered root vegetable grows sweeter in flavor after winter frosts and produces yellow flowers if left unharvested into its second season — name the vegetable?
Parsnip (Pastinaca sativa) is a root vegetable closely related to carrot and parsley, all belonging to the flowering plant family Apiaceae.
Prized as an ornamental indoor plant and still poorly understood taxonomically, this arum-family genus ranks second in size only to Anthurium — which genus?
Philodendron is a large genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae.
This birth defect results in extra fingers or toes, occurs more often in the hands than the feet, and has been linked to more than three dozen genetic mutations — what is it?
Polydactyly (commonly known as sixth finger and extra finger) is a birth defect that results in extra fingers or toes.

Also called blepharoptosis and sometimes mistakenly called 'lazy eye,' this condition is marked by the drooping of the upper lid over the eye and can affect vision development in children if untreated — what is it?
Ptosis (eyelid) is a drooping or falling of the upper eyelid.
This long-term autoimmune disorder leaves joints warm, swollen and painful — typically the same ones on both sides of the body — and can stiffen worse after rest. What is it?
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a long-term autoimmune disorder that primarily affects joints.

Native to the Azores, Europe, and the Middle East, this tree or shrub's flowers and berries have long been used for cordial and wine, and it also appears in traditional medicine and dietary supplements — name this plant?
Sambucus nigra is a temperate species of tree or shrub in the family Viburnaceae native to the Azores, Europe, and the Middle East.

Dubbed the "father of modern differential geometry," this Chinese-born American mathematician and poet won the Wolf Prize — and has a medal named for him by the International Mathematical Union. Who was he?
Shiing-Shen Chern (pinyin: Chn Xngshn; October 26, 1911 - December 3, 2004) was a Chinese-born American mathematician and poet.

Some versions allow a 'tie' or 'draw' while others insist on a single winner; it can pit hundreds against each other or just one person against the clock — what do we call this organized physical activity?
Sport is a physical activity or game, often competitive and organized, that maintains or improves physical ability and skills.
This West African berry contains a molecule that binds so powerfully to taste buds that sour foods eaten afterward taste sweet instead — what's this plant's common nickname?
Synsepalum dulcificum is a plant in the Sapotaceae family, native to tropical Africa.

One of five genera in the mackerel family whose members are collectively called tunas, this genus contains eight species, including the Atlantic bluefin, which can grow up to 15 feet long — name this genus?
Thunnus is a genus of ocean-dwelling, ray-finned bony fish from the mackerel family, Scombridae.
Caused by Salmonella Typhi bacteria and contracted orally, this disease presents with gradual fever, weakness, abdominal pain, and in severe cases, rose-colored skin spots. What is it?
Typhoid fever is an orally contracted disease caused by Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi bacteria, also called Salmonella Typhi.

In physics, this phenomenon occurs when two coherent waves combine according to their phase difference, producing either a boosted 'constructive' amplitude or a canceling 'destructive' one — what's the effect called?
Wave interference is a phenomenon in which two coherent waves are combined by adding their intensities or displacements with due consideration for their phase difference.
First synthesized by chemist Alexander Shulgin in 1974, this psychedelic compound produces hallucinogenic effects considered milder than LSD or psilocybin — what is it commonly known as?
2C-B: Psychedelic drug. 2C-B, also known as 4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine or by names such as Nexus or Erox, is a psychedelic drug of the phenethylamine and 2C families.
Also known as the buckeye or conker tree, this deciduous flowering tree is often confused with the unrelated sweet chestnut — which species?
Aesculus hippocastanum: Species of tree in the soapberry family.
Defined by at least one carbon-carbon triple bond and traditionally nicknamed for its simplest member, ethyne (better known as acetylene) — which class of hydrocarbon is this?
Alkyne: Hydrocarbon compound containing one or more C≡C bonds.
This scientific discipline uses techniques from titration to mass spectrometry to identify unknown compounds and measure exactly how much of each substance is present in a mixture - which field?
Analytical chemistry: Study of the separation, identification, and quantification of matter.
This psychological state describes a lack of feeling, motivation, or concern, sitting on a spectrum between normal drive and akinetic mutism — what is it called?
Apathy: State of indifference, or the suppression of emotions.
First described in 1740 under the name Compositae, this enormous flowering-plant family includes daisies, asters and sunflowers — what is it?
Asteraceae: Large family of flowering plants.
Named by naturalist Constantine Rafinesque in 1815, this predatory saltwater fish prowls near coral reefs and is a favorite target of sport anglers worldwide — what is it?

Having evolved independently at least 94 separate times — first in octocorals some 540 million years ago — this living glow lights up fireflies, deep-sea fish, fungi and dinoflagellates alike; what is it?
Bioluminescence: Emission of light by a living organism.
Also known as the penny bun or porcino, this prized edible fungus can grow a brown cap up to a foot wide and forms symbiotic partnerships with forest tree roots — which mushroom?
Boletus edulis: Species of mushroom, widely distributed in the Northern Hemisphere.
Bred in the 19th century as a guard dog by crossing the English Mastiff with the now-extinct Old English Bulldog, which large, short-muzzled English breed was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1924?
Bullmastiff: English breed of dog. The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
This Sicilian pastry is a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with sweet ricotta, dressed up with candied orange zest in Palermo or chopped pistachios in Catania — what treat is it?
Cannoli: Italian ricotta-filled pastry. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Native to the western Himalayas and the Mediterranean's high altitudes, this coniferous genus bears erect cones and wood that naturally repels moths — which genus?
Native to the high Andes and living in colonies called 'herds,' this South American rodent boasts the densest fur of any land mammal — about 20,000 hairs per square centimeter. What is it?
Chinchilla: Rodent genus. The chinchilla is named after the Chincha people of the Andes, who once wore its dense, velvet-like fur and ate its meat.
With a coat of dusky-grey blotches that inspired its common name, this wild cat is one of the few able to climb down tree trunks head-first, using a long tail for balance — what species is it?

Clouded leopard: Species of wild cat. Its head-and-body length ranges from 68.6 to 108 cm (27.0 to 42.5 in) with a 61 to 91 cm (24 to 36 in) long tail, which it uses for balancing when moving in trees.
Often defined as the transmission of information, this concept is famously modeled as a source encoding a message, sending it through a channel, and a receiver decoding it — what is it?
Communication: Transmission of information. Models of communication are simplified overviews of its main components and their interactions.
A group of these black birds is famously called a 'murder,' and their larger cousins are known as ravens — what bird is this?
Crow: Index of animals with the same common name.
The second jet fighter to enter RAF service and the first powered by a single jet engine, this twin-boom aircraft flew with the Halford Goblin turbojet — which aircraft?

De Havilland Vampire: Fighter aircraft; first single-engine jet in RAF service. The de Havilland DH100 Vampire is a British jet fighter developed and manufactured by the de Havilland Aircraft Company.
This category of mental health conditions involves an unconscious defense mechanism that fragments consciousness, memory, and identity to protect against traumatic stress — what is it called?
Dissociative disorder: Set of mental health conditions.
A pregnancy complication where the embryo attaches outside the uterus, classically presenting with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. What is this condition?
Ectopic pregnancy: Female reproductive system health issue.
A sympathomimetic stimulant often used to keep blood pressure up during anesthesia, this drug has also been tried for asthma, narcolepsy, and obesity — what is it?

Ranging from Northern Europe through Siberia to the Himalayas, this medium-sized wild cat is one of only four living species in its genus and can be found at elevations up to 5,500 meters — what animal is this?
Eurasian lynx: Species of medium-sized cat native to Eurasia.

Named for the physicist who reportedly asked 'but where is everybody?' at Los Alamos in 1950, this puzzle questions why we've found no evidence of alien civilizations despite the odds favoring them — what's it called?
Fermi paradox: Discrepancy of the lack of evidence for alien life despite its apparent likelihood.
Alongside James Watson, this English scientist co-authored the 1953 Nature paper unveiling DNA's double helix and later coined the phrase 'central dogma' — who is he?
Francis Crick: English physicist and biologist (1916–2004)

Published by Einstein in 1916 as a refinement of Newton's law of gravitation, this geometric framework describes gravity as curved spacetime, summed up by Wheeler as 'space-time tells matter how to move; matter tells space-time how to curve'?
General relativity: Theory of gravitation as curved spacetime. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Despite its common name, this Eurasian wolf-like canid is more closely related to wolves and coyotes than to its African namesakes — what animal is it?
Published in 1931 by an Austrian logician, these two results proved that any consistent axiom system for arithmetic will always contain true statements it cannot prove — what are they called?
Gödel's incompleteness theorems: Limitative results in mathematical logic.
Dubbed 'the Gauss of modern mathematics,' this French polymath's work on the three-body problem uncovered the first chaotic deterministic system, laying the groundwork for chaos theory — who is he?
Henri Poincaré: French mathematician, physicist and engineer (1854–1912)
With red compound eyes set wider apart in females, this insect lays batches of about 100 eggs on decaying matter that hatch into maggots — which species?
Housefly: Species of insect. The housefly (Musca domestica) is a fly of the suborder Cyclorrhapha.
Distinguished by the male's large, transversely ridged curved horns, which wild goat species roams Eurasia and Africa?
This order of crustaceans includes both seafaring gribbles and the woodlice in your garden, with females brooding their young in a belly pouch called a marsupium. What is it?
Isopoda: Order of arthropods. The order is divided into eleven suborders.

This American physicist worked with Niels Bohr on nuclear fission and had a gift for coinages — "quantum foam," "wormhole," and the term that popularized "gravitationally collapsed objects." Who was he?
John Archibald Wheeler: American theoretical physicist (1911–2008)
Nicknamed 'The Professor' on The Chase, this record-breaking contestant won 74 consecutive games on a legendary quiz show in 2004 before eventually becoming its host — who is he?
Ken Jennings: American game show host (born 1974)
Known by common names like true lavender and English lavender despite not being native to England, this Mediterranean-basin plant belongs to the mint family — which species?
Lavandula angustifolia: Species of plant. Lavandula angustifolia, formerly L. officinalis, is a flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, native to the Mediterranean basin.
A sweet, aromatic flavouring used in confectionery, tobacco, and pharmaceuticals comes from the root of which legume — though more than a couple of milligrams per kilo a day can cause trouble?
Painlessly swollen lymph nodes, drenching night sweats, and unexplained weight loss point to this family of white-blood-cell cancers, split mainly into Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin types — what is it?
Lymphoma: Hematologic cancer that affects lymphocytes.

The first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed as a university math professor, this Milanese scholar later traded calculus for four decades of theology and charity — who is she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi: Italian mathematician and philanthropist (1718–1799)
Typically running 21 to 35 days, this coordinated dance of estrogen and progesterone prepares the uterine lining and releases an egg to make pregnancy possible — what is it?
Menstrual cycle: Natural changes in the human female reproductive system.
Based on a Soviet fighter jet but optimized for ground attack, this variable-sweep aircraft was license-built in India as the 'Bahadur,' or 'Valiant' — which jet?
Mikoyan MiG-27: Series of 1970s Soviet attack aircraft.
Born in China and educated at MIT and Stanford, this billionaire engineer founded Taiwan's dominant chipmaker, serving as its CEO from 1987 to 2005 — who is he?
Morris Chang: Taiwanese businessman and electrical engineer (born 1931)
This chronic neurological disorder scrambles the sleep-wake cycle, bringing on excessive daytime sleepiness, sleep paralysis, and sudden episodes of muscle collapse called cataplexy — what is it?
Narcolepsy: Human sleep disorder. Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that impairs the ability to regulate sleep–wake cycles, and specifically impacts REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.

Usually made from unleavened dough that's rolled, cut, or extruded into long strips, this staple food is called pasta in Italian cuisine and split into wheat-based and starch-based varieties in Chinese cooking — what is it?
Noodle: Staple food made from unleavened dough, commonly long and thin.
Discovered by naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace in 1859, this fungus hijacks carpenter ants' brains and marches them down to the forest floor before killing them — which organism?

Ophiocordyceps unilateralis: Species of fungus. Ophiocordyceps unilateralis, commonly known as zombie-ant fungus, is an insect-pathogenic fungus, discovered by the British naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace in 1859.
First domesticated in Mesoamerica and led in production today by India, this tropical fruit belongs to the small genus Carica — what is it?
Papaya: Species of tropical fruit plant.
This inflammation of the sac surrounding the heart causes sharp chest pain that eases when sitting up and worsens when lying down or breathing deeply — what condition is it?
Pericarditis: Inflammation of the pericardium. Pericarditis (PER-i-kar-DYE-tis) is inflammation of the pericardium, the fibrous sac surrounding the heart.
Boasting the longest cones of any spruce and widely planted as a Christmas tree, this European conifer was also the first gymnosperm to have its genome sequenced — which species?
Picea abies: Species of plant. Picea abies, the Norway spruce, Norway fir or European spruce, is a species of spruce native to Northern, Central and Eastern Europe.
Born Joseph Ratzinger, this head of the Catholic Church made history in 2013 by resigning the role, then adopted the title 'emeritus' until his death — who was he?
Pope Benedict XVI: Head of the Catholic Church from 2005 to 2013.

With 348 known species spanning an opportunistic human pathogen, a plant disease-causer, and a soil-dwelling growth-promoter, which gram-negative bacterial genus in Gammaproteobacteria is renowned for its metabolic diversity?
Pseudomonas: Genus of Gram-negative bacteria. Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
This Norwegian shared the very first Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics, and we owe him the words 'econometrics,' 'microeconomics,' and 'macroeconomics' — who was he?
Ragnar Frisch: Norwegian economist and Nobel Laureate (1895–1973)
Native to Europe, northwestern Africa, and southwestern Asia, this flowering shrub's edible fruit stars in desserts and preserves — what's its species name, better known as the gooseberry?
Ribes uva-crispa: Species of flowering plant in the family Grossulariaceae.
Introduced in the 1970s, this database language let programmers grab many records with one single command, eliminating the need to specify an index path to reach each one — what is it?

Originally from the Mediterranean, this yellowish-gray arthropod has up to 15 pairs of long legs and preys on insects with venom too mild to harm humans — what species commonly invades homes worldwide?
Scutigera coleoptrata: Species of arthropod. Scutigera coleoptrata, also known as the house centipede, is a species of centipede that is typically yellowish-gray and has up to 15 pairs of long legs.
Better known by the brand name Viagra, this drug treats erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension, kicking in within about twenty minutes — what is it?

Sildenafil: Drug for erectile dysfunction and hypertension. Sildenafil, sold under the brand name Viagra among others, is a medication used to treat erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Native to East Asia and the world's most-grown legume, this crop becomes everything from edamame and tofu to soy sauce, nattō and tempeh — what is it?
Soybean: Legume grown for its edible bean.
Named from Greek words for 'twisted' and 'grain,' this genus of spherical bacteria divides along a single axis to form chains, unlike its grape-cluster-forming cousins — coined in 1877, what is it?
Streptococcus: Genus of bacteria. In 1984, many bacteria formerly grouped in the genus Streptococcus were separated out into the genera Enterococcus and Lactococcus.
The lone species in its genus, this African-born leguminous tree gives pods of sweet-tangy pulp used in cuisines worldwide, plus a seed oil and even a dye — what is it?
Tamarind: Leguminous tree bearing edible fruit.

Comprising two Einstein-authored physics frameworks published in 1905 and 1915 — one covering phenomena without gravity, the other explaining gravitation itself — this pair introduced four-dimensional spacetime and superseded Newtonian mechanics. Which pair of physics frameworks is this?
Theory of relativity: Two interrelated physics theories by Albert Einstein.
This shelled reptile retracts its head and neck straight back into its shell for protection, with the largest species growing over a metre long and weighing more than 100 kilograms — what is it?
Named from the Greek word for cheese after being first isolated from casein in 1846, this amino acid carries the one-letter code Y — what is it?
Tyrosine: Amino acid. L-Tyrosine or tyrosine (symbol Tyr or Y) or 4-hydroxyphenylalanine is one of the 20 standard amino acids that are used by cells to synthesize proteins.

The northernmost marsupial on Earth, this cat-sized nocturnal opportunist is a familiar visitor to trash cans and compost piles across North America, and often ends up as roadkill due to its slow pace — what is it?
Virginia opossum: Species of North American marsupial.
Aboard Apollo 8, the first crewed mission to leave low Earth orbit, this astronaut snapped the iconic "Earthrise" photograph as the crew circled the Moon ten times — who took it?
William Anders: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1933–2024)
The symbol for seaborgium is Sg. Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
The symbol for lanthanum is La. Lanthanum is a chemical element; it has symbol La and atomic number 57.

Pick the comedian from these four.
George Lopez is a comedian. George Edward Lopez (born April 23, 1961) is an American stand-up comedian and actor.
In what year was Judy Garland born?
Judy Garland (born Frances Ethel Gumm; June 10, 1922 – June 22, 1969) was an American actress, singer, and vaudevillian whose career spanned four decades.
In what year was Hugh Grant born?
Hugh Grant: Hugh John Mungo Grant (born 9 September 1960) is an English actor.
In what year was Martin Sheen born?
Martin Sheen: Ramón Gerard Antonio Estévez (born August 3, 1940), known professionally as Martin Sheen, is an American actor.
In what year was Billy Bob Thornton born?
Billy Bob Thornton (born August 4, 1955) is an American actor, filmmaker, screenwriter, and singer-songwriter.
